q: Estimate the solute potential of the solution that causes no change in mass.
Deduce the water potential of the beetroot tissue. Explain.
About -0.70 MPa. No net water movement means the tissue and the solution have equal water potential; an open solution has no pressure potential, so its water potential equals its solute potential.
The cells have a pressure potential of +0.4 MPa at the start. Calculate their solute potential.
Water potential = solute potential + pressure potential, so solute potential = -0.70 − 0.4 = -1.1 MPa.
In pure water the discs gain mass, but only about 14%. Explain why the gain stops.
Water enters by osmosis and the cells swell, but the cell wall pushes back: pressure potential rises until the water potential inside equals 0, so net entry stops.
Explain why five discs were used at each concentration.
Discs vary; a mean of five is more reliable, and the SD shows whether differences between solutions are bigger than the variation.
